event: Tie Bo hears her out, and then he answers, flat and slow, one thing at a time.

changes.note: New bond: Tie Bo 4 (she agreed to come, heard him, shared her reading, asked of poison)

event: "Poison. There's one poison in Three Stones. Granny Hua keeps aconite, for rats."

memory.fact: Aconite is the only strong poison in Three Stones; there is no other in the village or the market.
Aconite is the only strong poison in Three Stones; there is no other in the village or the market.

event: "A boiled paste of it, for a dog gone mad. There's no other poison in the village."

memory.fact: Granny Hua keeps aconite, or wolfsbane, for rats, and a boiled paste of it for dogs gone mad.
Granny Hua keeps aconite, or wolfsbane, for rats, and a boiled paste of it for dogs gone mad.

event: "I'd take it if she gave it. Soak the stakes with it, and soak the bait."

memory.fact: Tie Bo would take poison if offered, and would soak the stakes and the bait with it.
Tie Bo would take poison if offered, and would soak the stakes and the bait with it.

event: "But it's hers, and she'll not hand it to me. Maybe not to the headman either."
"A pit in the paddy? No. It would fill with mud and water before midnight."
"Besides, the terraces are the village's rice. The headman would never allow a dig there."

memory.fact: Paddy earth is too soft and wet to hold a pit's walls, and the terraces are the village's rice.
Paddy earth is too soft and wet to hold a pit's walls, and the terraces are the village's rice.

event: "Up at the wallow, maybe. But that ground is bog, and it's his own wallow besides."

memory.fact: A pit by the wallow could work, but the ground there is bog and the boar's own wallow besides.
A pit by the wallow could work, but the ground there is bog and the boar's own wallow besides.

event: "Fire? We have straw, pine resin and green bamboo, and all three smoke thick."

memory.fact: Straw, pine resin and green bamboo smoke thickly, and the village has all three in plenty.
Straw, pine resin and green bamboo smoke thickly, and the village has all three in plenty.

event: "But smoke in an open pit just rises away. A beast that can walk out isn't smothered."

memory.fact: Smoke in an open pit would rise away; a beast that can leave is not suffocated by it.
Smoke in an open pit would rise away; a beast that can leave is not suffocated by it.

event: "And fire in those pines would run the whole valley. Terraces, houses, the lot."

memory.fact: Fire in dry pine woods would run up the valley and take the terraces and the village with it.
Fire in dry pine woods would run up the valley and take the terraces and the village with it.

event: "The headman would forbid it, and he'd be right. And I'd not do it anyway."

memory.fact: Gu would forbid fire in the woods above the terraces, and any dig that could let water into them.
Gu would forbid fire in the woods above the terraces, and any dig that could let water into them.

event: "A burning, blinded boar is worse than a whole one."

memory.fact: Tie Bo would rather not smoke it: a blinded, burning boar is worse than a whole one.
Tie Bo would rather not smoke it: a blinded, burning boar is worse than a whole one.

event: He is quiet a moment, looking at the lamp, and then he says what he has been holding back.
"I'll not promise you we kill it. I'll promise to make it bleed and leave the rice alone."

memory.fact: Tie Bo would not promise to kill it, only to make it bleed and leave the terraces alone.
Tie Bo would not promise to kill it, only to make it bleed and leave the terraces alone.

event: "This bow is mulberry. Good on a deer. It will not touch a hide like that one's."

memory.fact: Tie Bo's bow is of mulberry wood, good against deer and no use against a hide like this one.
Tie Bo's bow is of mulberry wood, good against deer and no use against a hide like this one.

event: "There are the headman's two old iron-headed spears. I'll ask two men I trust to stand with me."

memory.fact: Tie Bo would ask two more men he trusts besides the Fangs, and arm them with boar spears.
Tie Bo would ask two more men he trusts besides the Fangs, and arm them with boar spears.
The headman keeps two old iron-headed spears in his house against bandits.
The headman keeps two old iron-headed spears in his house against bandits.

event: "How old would a boar be, to weigh what that one weighs? Old. And cunning with it."

memory.fact: The village reckons a boar old enough to be this size must be many years old and cunning.
The village reckons a boar old enough to be this size must be many years old and cunning.

event: "Old boars have smelled smoke and heard dogs and seen men. They are not fooled twice."

memory.fact: A boar that old has smelled smoke, heard dogs and seen men before, and is not fooled twice.
A boar that old has smelled smoke, heard dogs and seen men before, and is not fooled twice.

event: "My grandfather told a story about that." He looks up at the dark hills.
"A white stag lived on the mountain, and three hunters went up after it."
"It killed all three of them, and they never once drew blood."

memory.fact: Tie Bo's grandfather told of a white stag in the hills that killed three hunters and took no spear.
Tie Bo's grandfather told of a white stag in the hills that killed three hunters and took no spear.

event: "It went through the pines like smoke."
"Then a wanderer came and burned a bundle of herbs at the shrine here, at the Three Stones."

memory.fact: In that tale the stag left when a wanderer burned a bundle of herbs at the village shrine.
In that tale the stag left when a wanderer burned a bundle of herbs at the village shrine.

event: "The stag went higher up the mountain that night, and nobody has hunted it since."

memory.fact: The old stag tale ends with the stag living on the mountain, and nobody hunting it again.
The old stag tale ends with the stag living on the mountain, and nobody hunting it again.

event: "The wanderer was a cultivator, and the village paid him a year's rice for it."

memory.fact: In that tale the wanderer was a cultivator, and the village paid him a year's rice for it.
In that tale the wanderer was a cultivator, and the village paid him a year's rice for it.

event: "Steel will not bite a spirit beast. Everybody knows that much."

memory.fact: Village tales hold that steel will not bite a spirit beast's hide, arrow or spear alike.
Village tales hold that steel will not bite a spirit beast's hide, arrow or spear alike.

event: "So if it is one, spears will not kill it. We will only make it bleed."
"And they say a beast newly stirred is the worst kind. Hungry, half wild, not afraid of men."

memory.fact: Folk say a beast newly stirred is worst, being hungry, half wild, and still unafraid of men.
Folk say a beast newly stirred is worst, being hungry, half wild, and still unafraid of men.

event: "And a wounded one turns into a terror. It hunts whoever cut it."

memory.fact: Folk say a wounded spirit beast becomes a terror, and hunts whoever cut it.
Folk say a wounded spirit beast becomes a terror, and hunts whoever cut it.

event: He settles the bow on his shoulder. "It's still my brother's boar. I'll go up with a spear."
"Tomorrow at dusk. The Fangs uphill with torches and gongs. Me behind the stakes."
"You stand behind us, out of the line, and tell me what you see."
"The poison, or whatever she keeps, is Granny Hua's."
"She bars her door at night, and she'll not deal with anyone she hasn't seen by daylight."

memory.fact: Granny Hua bars her door at night, and will not deal with anyone she has not seen by daylight.
Granny Hua bars her door at night, and will not deal with anyone she has not seen by daylight.

event: "She'll want your hand in hers, and a good look at your face in the sun. That's her way."

memory.fact: Granny Hua holds her doubts until she has seen the stranger by daylight and touched her hand.
Granny Hua holds her doubts until she has seen the stranger by daylight and touched her hand.

event: Up at the headman's gate a lamp burns; Zhao Jun is in there telling all of it, as he was told.
Tie Bo looks at her one last time. "Tomorrow morning, then. Will you come to her door with me?"

memory.fact: At night by the shrine, Tie Bo asked Nala to come with him to Granny Hua's door in the morning.
At night by the shrine, Tie Bo asked Nala to come with him to Granny Hua's door in the morning.
